title: Decode stream coordination and capture heuristics for stable CUDA graphs and replay
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Intermittent incorrect outputs and nondeterministic hangs observed when capturing and replaying CUDA graphs for multi-stream decode workloads. Root causes suspected: capture window misalignment between prefill and decode streams, transient pointer/allocator differences invalidating captured graphs, and racey kernel ordering for fused attention kernels when streams are reused.

Goal: Implement defensive capture heuristics, lightweight runtime coordination primitives, and a deterministic replay fallback so graph replay is stable across concurrent decode workloads without regressing latency for common paths. Deliverables: (1) capture heuristics that avoid invalidation in common failure modes, (2) stream coordination layer to ensure safe reuse, (3) deterministic replay mode for regression testing and emergency fallback, (4) validations and perf benchmarks with real workload traces.
acceptance_criteria: Replays of captured graphs for multi-stream 8k and 32k token sequences produce bit-identical outputs (or within float-tolerance for fp16/fp8) for 99.9% of traces compared to non-graph execution.
No increase in P50 latency >5% for 95% of traffic under the new heuristics in A/B tests on staging clusters.
Capture invalidation rate (graphs dropped due to allocator/shape/pointer mismatch) reduced by >=80% for observed production traces.
Deterministic replay mode available behind a config flag with telemetry (replay_success, replay_fallback_reason) emitted to console and internal metrics.
Automated tests covering pointer aliasing, mixed batch shapes, kv cache reuse, and interleaved prefill/decode are added to CI.
tasks: Instrument capture pipeline to log capture triggers, allocator fingerprints, and memory base pointers (low-overhead sampling) — work with observability team to add metrics
Implement capture-safety checks: allocator-fingerprint, stream-epoch, and sequence-length-bucket validation before replay
Introduce lightweight stream coordination API (acquire_release semantics) to serialize prefill and first-decode capture sequences when necessary
Add a graph-warmup path that performs a short deterministic warmup run when a graph is first created to ensure kernels compiled/linked consistently
Implement deterministic-replay fallback that runs on CPU/naive kernels if replay fails more than N times, and emits debug artifacts
Add unit & integration tests for pointer aliasing, fused-attention kernel ordering, and mixed-precision edgecases
Run staging canary with trace-based workloads from customers A/B testing and collect replay success/failure telemetry
Review and performance-tune kernel launch ordering and stream synchronization to minimize latency impact of coordination primitives
test_plan: Unit tests for allocator-fingerprint mismatch detection (simulate different base pointers)
Integration test: multi-stream decoder fixture with interleaved prefill and decode across 4 concurrent streams, assert no deadlock and output correctness
Regression suite comparing graph vs non-graph outputs across 100 real traces sampled from production; threshold checks for numeric tolerance
Perf benchmark: compare p50/p95 token latency and throughput before/after heuristics on a 8xA100 staging cluster
Chaos test: force allocator churn, simulate prefill interruption, verify fallback & telemetry
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime flag 'graph_replay_safety_v2' — default off in prod
Step 1: Enable on internal staging clusters and run nightly regression traces for 72 hours
Step 2: Canary to 2% of hosted traffic with telemetry gating (replay_success > 99.5%)
Step 3: Increase to 25% if canary stable for 48 hours, revert if customer-impacting regressions observed
Step 4: Flip default to on for runtime-1.20 and include safe fallback thresholds
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Coordination primitives could increase tail latency under high-concurrency. Mitigation: adaptive heuristics — only serialize when fingerprint checks fail or for cold graphs; add metrics to detect regressions
Risk: Fingerprint collisions could cause unnecessary fallbacks. Mitigation: combine allocator fingerprint with model-config hash and sequence-length-bucket; keep sampling low-overhead
Risk: Deterministic replay may be slower and expose new bugs. Mitigation: keep it as emergency fallback and enable extensive CI coverage before release
notes: Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/GRAPH-REPLAY-SAFETY (internal); see section 'Allocator fingerprint and stream epoch'
Related ticket ENG-31107 has prior deterministic replay prototypes — coordinate on test fixtures
Spike findings: pointer-based invalidations occurred when using custom pool allocator with deferred frees; adding base-pointer check reduced failures in trace 14 by 95%
comments: 2025-02-11 — Maya Chen: Started spike. Reproduced nondeterministic outputs on trace set 'gptx-mix-1' with 3 concurrent streams. Root cause looks like stream reuse changing kernel launch order for fused attention kernels.

2025-02-14 — Ravi Patel: Implemented first pass allocator-fingerprint and simple stream-epoch check. Local CI shows reduced failures but a 3% p95 tail regression — investigating coordination granularity.
2025-02-18 — PM review (Lara Gomez): Confirmed customer-impact priority high; requested telemetry keys: replay_success, replay_failure_reason, capture_invalidation_count.
2025-02-21 — Design Review (Jonas Meyer): Approved stream coordination API but asked for fallback to be non-disruptive (no hard OOM or hangs). Suggested warmup-run to stabilize kernels.

2025-02-24 — Ravi Patel: Added deterministic-replay mode behind flag and wire telemetry. Manual staging run: replay_success=99.2% on 24h sample; failures due to mixed batch shape edgecases — added shape normalization filter

2025-02-28 — Maya Chen: Prepared PR for review to introduce capture-safety checks and lightweight coordination primitives. Requesting review from infra and perf teams. Next: CI test coverage and staging canary
